methods.daily_volume: Original decimal daily mean discharge summed exactly before multiplication by 0.028316846592 m3/ft3 and 86400 nominal seconds/day.
methods.completeness: Complete period volume requires every selected calendar date to contain a numeric original value. Observed-period volume retains only known days and is never annualized.
methods.flags: A and e may coexist. Approved, provisional, estimated and revised flags are separate preserved source attributes; record flags include nonnumeric observations.
methods.seasons: Winter is January, February and December of the same calendar year. Spring is March–May, summer June–August, autumn September–November. These disjoint month groups partition each complete calendar year.
methods.fractions: Annual fractions require a complete numeric calendar year and positive annual volume. Monthly/seasonal profile means weight each eligible complete year equally; separately retained fully approved profiles use only years with A on every numeric day.
methods.duration: Qp is the R-7 observed daily quantile at 1-p/100. Thus Q5 is P95 and Q95 is P05. Curves describe retained numeric days; incomplete years are explicitly labelled.
methods.thresholds: High-flow tail includes days at or above the observed P95; low-flow tail includes days at or below P10. Ties may make those day fractions exceed 5% or 10%. Full dated original positions are retained.
methods.comparison: Each selected-year comparison uses other complete calendar periods at the same gauge, independently of annual completeness, with separate complete-numeric and fully-approved reference choices. Mean ratios compare daily mean discharge; volume ratios also retain actual calendar length, including leap February. Annual-volume fraction comparisons use a separate complete-annual-year cohort. Missing target/reference support returns null.
methods.scope: Gauge discharge is hydrologic context. It is not a nutrient/sediment load or model calibration fit. Gauge volumes are not summed across stations; upstream/downstream catchments and regulated or diverted flows retain their own identities.
